items.recapEn: At Ōiso on a hot July evening Hana counted two old boats, three people and five round white stones. Katō-san, whose family owns the boats, gave them two bottles of cold tea, and Hana drew a third circle in her kindness tally. A blue-grey cat sat under a boat: Ao, said Hana; not Ao, said Ken.

items.recapEn: On the beach Hana greets Katō-san and asks whether there are many people; not on a summer evening, she says. The old boat is her family's. She offers cold tea from a box of five bottles and gives them two. Hana asks about a cat: a blue-grey one sits under the boat every day. Ao, says Hana; Ken disagrees.

items.recapEn: A hand-written notice by the boats at Ōiso lists what is in Katō-san's blue lost-property box: one black umbrella, two white hats, three handkerchiefs, a single child's right shoe, glasses, a watch and a difficult book, but no wallet or key. She is there from five to six every evening; so is a blue-grey cat that belongs to nobody.
